"""B3 installed capture: open to first presented result and indexed PSS for one million-file search.

One run launches the exact `flea --gui` launcher on a census-bound corpus, types the search key and
query through real Wayland input as soon as the window maps, and reads the same process's
flea.searchStamps. The first result time is the compositor's presentation time of the first
submitted frame that painted the query's own rows (CLOCK_MONOTONIC, wp_presentation), minus the
launch time on the same clock. PSS is the sum of smaps_rollup over every live process of the run's
cgroup except the driver itself, sampled once the answer settled on a complete index. A missing
seam, a partial or mismatched index, a foreign process or a failed close blocks the run; nothing
is estimated. Exit 0 validated capture, 3 blocked, 2 bad input. See README.md.

"""Writes the benchmark charts in docs/images/ from the release-candidate bench CSVs.

    tools/flea-bench-chart                 rewrites the six files in docs/images/
    tools/flea-bench-chart /tmp/out        writes somewhere else, for a diff

Two charts, each in two cuts. The wide SVG is for the README, where GitHub renders it in both
themes, so it paints its own opaque ground and carries no script, no SMIL and no CSS animation for
the markdown sanitiser to strip. The narrow one is cropped for social and is authored at a 600 px
logical width, so the artboard's own type sizes land at their native size when it is displayed at
600 px, then rendered to PNG at 2x.

Every value is read out of `tools/flea-bench-report`, which derives it from the CSV and its
manifest. Nothing here retypes a CSV cell, because four documentation counts on this branch were
wrong after being corrected by somebody counting declaration lines.

The design is docs/reference/flea-canvas/Bench.dc.html, one of the 17 artboards, and where that
board's prose and its artwork disagree the artwork is the specification.
"""

The method is tools/flea-field-nav's, which is tools/flea-field-search's: tools/flea-framecap records which presented
frames change inside a rectangle, stamped with the compositor's presentation time in CLOCK_MONOTONIC, and every input
(key, button, wheel notch, touchpad stroke) goes to a uinput device stamped in CLOCK_MONOTONIC just before the write.
A sample is the input to the first frame in which the watched region changes with ink (first_ms, the number the
budget judges), beside the first change of any kind (first_any_ms) and the last change before a quiet gap (settled_ms).
A key that changes nothing before the next input is a miss and counts as over every limit, never as a dropped sample.

Ops (row 6). The backend runs one write at a time and refuses a second as an error line, and the status bar draws only the
oldest unacknowledged error, so a paste that starts under a running job or a queued error draws nothing of its own. Every op
sample therefore starts on an idle status bar: statusActivityState (ui/Ipc.qml) is read, Esc dismisses each queued error and
cancels a running transfer, and a bar that is not clear inside 20 s ends the sample with an error row, never a timing. A
paste that does not finish inside its wait (120 s, 900 s for op.copy.long) is cancelled with Esc and given 60 s to leave
the activity list before the next sample. Each op row carries errors_before and errors_after (queued errors), activity_after
(the activities still up), notice_before and notice_after (the status notice before and after the paste), esc_before (Escs
the bar needed before the paste) and refused, true when the paste left more queued errors than it found; the report counts
refused samples beside the misses.

The method is tools/flea-field-search's: tools/flea-framecap stamps the frames that differ in a rectangle in CLOCK_MONOTONIC, and keys go to the ydotool socket stamped in CLOCK_MONOTONIC just before the write, so key and frame share one clock.
This tool imports that file (SourceFileLoader, no copy) and reuses its detector, input path, recorder, launch lines, regions and report maths.
Columns time the keystroke to the first frame in which the entrant's content region changes (first) and to the last change before 2 s of quiet, cap 15 s (settled).
The columns are nav.cursor.inview.<view> (one untimed Down, quiet, then 7 timed Downs at a 400 ms pace inside the first screen) and nav.cursor.scroll.<view> (Downs past the bottom edge, quiet, then 12 timed Downs that each scroll).
The columns go on with nav.enter.<view> and nav.back.<view> (one Down selects the folder, quiet, Enter into its 1000 entries, quiet, the back key out) and preview.<kind> (quicklook: Space on the file; pane: the Down that lands on it, watched in the right 40 percent of the content region, refined per entrant with explore).
The ql column times Quick Look on a 4096 byte Markdown document that opens with a 40-row table (ql_md_table_first) against a tableless one of the same size (ql_md_plain), each in a launch of its own so every sample is a first open, key to settled_ms; a byte-identical twin (ql_md_plain_b) is the negative control.
report prints INCOMPLETE with no twin rows, INVALID when the twin control reports INSTRUMENT-NOISE, else SHIP when p95(table) <= p95(plain) + the control's own gap |p95(plain) - p95(twin)|, else HOLD.
An entrant without the preview feature gets a "no feature" row, never a silent gap.
